$comment: Generated by node contract/tools/generate.mjs. Edit contract/tools, not these files.
notes: grammars pins resolveGrammar (section 15.1); commandLines pins serialize (15.2); classifications pins classify (15.4); walks pins walk and statusBudgets pins statusBudget (15.5); hosts, users and ports pin hostForm, isUser and isPort (15.6).
A command line is compared byte for byte. A refusal is null line, the code, and the index of the refused element, or null when the whole argv or line is refused.

classifications inputs are the evidence of one attempt. sshLog is the text ssh wrote with -E; one trailing CR is removed from each line before the patterns are tried. Android, which has no ssh log, runs the cases whose sshLog is empty and launchFailed is false.
A walk result is what classify returns for that attempt, or a badRequest failure for a line section 15.2 refused. sent lists the indices of the attempts made.
Cases tagged injection are strings that try to be ssh options, shell syntax or known_hosts patterns; the document guard in common.schema.json refuses them as well.

grammars.name: linux-posix
grammars.purpose: A Linux system with its shell written out: that value is the grammar.

grammars.name: linux-shell-absent
grammars.purpose: No shell on a Linux system: a POSIX shell is what its OpenSSH runs.

grammars.name: platform-and-shell-absent
grammars.purpose: Neither platform nor shell: anything that is not Windows defaults to POSIX.

grammars.name: mac-shell-absent
grammars.purpose: A Mac with no shell is a POSIX login like Linux.

grammars.name: windows-shell-absent
grammars.purpose: No shell on Windows: cmd, because that is what a stock Windows OpenSSH runs. The Mac guessed PowerShell here and the desktop cmd, so one setup was quoted two ways (C4).

grammars.name: windows-restricted-false
grammars.purpose: restricted false changes nothing: a Windows system without a shell is still cmd.

grammars.name: windows-powershell
grammars.purpose: An account whose OpenSSH runs PowerShell says so; it is never inferred.

grammars.name: linux-cmd-written
grammars.purpose: A shell that is written out wins over the platform, even an odd one: the document says how the line is read.

grammars.name: restricted-in-document
grammars.purpose: A system restricted in the document uses the dispatcher grammar whatever its shell: the forced command is not a shell, on any platform (C4).

grammars.name: restricted-session-reported
grammars.purpose: The last authenticated status over this route reported a restricted session: dispatch, whatever the document says.

grammars.name: restricted-session-three-elements
grammars.purpose: The dispatcher runs exactly an interpreter and an entry. A third element would be an agent argument smuggled in front of every command, so the system is refused.

grammars.name: restricted-one-element
grammars.purpose: One element is not interpreter and entry either: refused like three.

grammars.name: restricted-wins-over-unknown-shell
grammars.purpose: Restriction is decided before the shell is read, so a shell value nobody knows does not matter on a restricted system.

grammars.name: pwsh-unknown
grammars.purpose: pwsh is not a grammar name. Aliases are refused, never mapped to the nearest grammar.

grammars.name: shell-case-sensitive
grammars.purpose: Grammar names are compared exactly; POSIX in capitals is not posix.

grammars.name: restricted-null
grammars.purpose: Only the JSON value true restricts a system; null does not.

commandLines.name: posix-launcher-status
commandLines.purpose: The everyday line: every element is in the bare set, so nothing is quoted.

commandLines.name: posix-space-in-path
commandLines.purpose: A path with a space is single-quoted as one element; the bare elements around it stay bare.

commandLines.name: posix-sh-c-exec
commandLines.purpose: The enrolment fetch command: the script for sh -c is one element, quoted so the remote shell passes it to sh untouched and sh expands $HOME itself.

commandLines.name: posix-single-quote
commandLines.purpose: A single quote inside an element closes the quoted run, adds an escaped quote and reopens it: '\''.

commandLines.name: posix-tilde-never-bare
commandLines.purpose: A tilde is never bare. argv elements are literal, and a shell would expand ~ where the dispatcher does not, so the same document would name two different files.

commandLines.name: posix-assignment-first
commandLines.purpose: An = in the first word makes sh read it as a variable assignment and run the next word instead, so the first element is quoted.

commandLines.name: posix-leading-equals
commandLines.purpose: A word starting with = is expanded by zsh to the path of a command, so it is quoted.

commandLines.name: posix-option-with-value
commandLines.purpose: An = after the first character of a later element is plain text to every supported shell and stays bare.

commandLines.name: posix-backslash-letter
commandLines.purpose: A backslash before a letter is literal inside single quotes in every supported shell, fish included.

commandLines.name: posix-double-backslash
commandLines.purpose: Two backslashes are one to fish inside single quotes, so the element cannot be written for every POSIX shell the same way.

commandLines.name: posix-trailing-backslash
commandLines.purpose: A trailing backslash would escape the closing quote in fish.

commandLines.name: posix-backslash-quote
commandLines.purpose: A backslash before a quote is an escaped quote to fish inside single quotes.

commandLines.name: posix-empty-element
commandLines.purpose: An empty element vanishes or becomes an empty argument depending on the shell; it is refused in every grammar.

commandLines.name: posix-line-feed
commandLines.purpose: A line feed ends the command in a shell and splits the dispatcher line; no grammar carries a control character.

commandLines.name: posix-delete-character
commandLines.purpose: U+007F is a control character too.

commandLines.name: posix-non-ascii
commandLines.purpose: Anything outside the bare set is quoted, non-ASCII letters included; the bytes inside the quotes are passed as they are.

commandLines.name: posix-metacharacters
commandLines.purpose: Every character a POSIX shell treats as syntax is literal inside single quotes.

commandLines.name: posix-no-command
commandLines.purpose: An empty argv has nothing to run. A system that is not driven never reaches the serialiser; this is the second guard.

commandLines.name: dispatch-windows-paths
commandLines.purpose: A restricted Windows system: its backslashes are quoted, because the dispatcher refuses a bare backslash. Android left them bare and could not drive one (C4).

commandLines.name: dispatch-restricted-run
commandLines.purpose: A helper running a wake action through a restricted key: interpreter, launcher, command, all bare.

commandLines.name: dispatch-unc-path
commandLines.purpose: A UNC path is quoted and accepted: the dispatcher takes everything inside quotes literally, so the fish backslash rule does not apply.

commandLines.name: dispatch-trailing-backslash
commandLines.purpose: A trailing backslash is fine for the dispatcher, which has no escapes inside quotes.

commandLines.name: dispatch-single-quote
commandLines.purpose: The dispatcher's one escape: \' outside quotes is a literal quote, so the POSIX spelling works unchanged.

commandLines.name: dispatch-empty-element
commandLines.purpose: An empty element is refused in the dispatcher grammar as well.

commandLines.name: dispatch-64-elements
commandLines.purpose: Exactly 64 elements: the most the dispatcher accepts.

expect.line: node /home/me/.legion-control/bin/launcher.mjs a0 a1 a2 a3 a4 a5 a6 a7 a8 a9 a10 a11 a12 a13 a14 a15 a16 a17 a18 a19 a20 a21 a22 a23 a24 a25 a26 a27 a28 a29 a30 a31 a32 a33 a34 a35 a36 a37 a38 a39 a40 a41 a42 a43 a44 a45 a46 a47 a48 a49 a50 a51 a52 a53 a54 a55 a56 a57 a58 a59 a60 a61

commandLines.name: dispatch-65-elements
commandLines.purpose: One element over the dispatcher limit: refused before anything is written.

commandLines.name: dispatch-4096-byte-element
commandLines.purpose: An element of exactly 4096 UTF-8 bytes: the longest the dispatcher takes.

commandLines.name: dispatch-4097-byte-element
commandLines.purpose: One byte over: refused, with the index of the element.

commandLines.name: dispatch-16384-byte-line
commandLines.purpose: A line of exactly 16384 UTF-8 bytes: the longest the dispatcher reads.

commandLines.name: dispatch-16385-byte-line
commandLines.purpose: One byte longer: refused as a whole line.

commandLines.name: dispatch-65-elements-one-empty
commandLines.purpose: Too many elements, the last of them empty: the count is checked before any element, so the refusal is the whole argv and names no index.

commandLines.name: dispatch-long-line-long-element
commandLines.purpose: An element over 4096 bytes in a line over 16384: elements are checked first and the line only after all of them, so the element is named.

commandLines.name: cmd-program-files-x86
commandLines.purpose: Every cmd element is double-quoted and the line starts with @. Parentheses are literal inside quotes; carets inside quotes are literal too, which is why the desktop broke this path by adding them (D10). The @ survives cmd /c whether or not sshd wrapped the line in quotes (A12).

commandLines.name: cmd-trailing-backslash
commandLines.purpose: A trailing backslash is doubled, so the C runtime reads one backslash and a closing quote rather than an escaped quote.

commandLines.name: cmd-trailing-backslash-run
commandLines.purpose: The whole trailing run is doubled: two backslashes become four. Backslashes anywhere else stand for themselves.

commandLines.name: cmd-operators-inside-quotes
commandLines.purpose: & | < > and ^ are literal inside double quotes; no caret is added.

commandLines.name: cmd-percent
commandLines.purpose: cmd expands %VAR% even inside quotes, so a percent sign cannot be carried.

commandLines.name: cmd-exclamation
commandLines.purpose: With delayed expansion on, cmd expands !VAR! inside quotes; an exclamation mark is refused.

commandLines.name: cmd-double-quote
commandLines.purpose: A double quote cannot be written inside a cmd line that both cmd and the C runtime read the same way.

commandLines.name: cmd-empty-element
commandLines.purpose: An empty element is refused in cmd as everywhere.

commandLines.name: cmd-line-feed
commandLines.purpose: A carriage return or line feed would end the cmd line.

commandLines.name: cmd-encoded-powershell
commandLines.purpose: The enrolment fetch on Windows: an encoded PowerShell command run from cmd. + / and = in the base64 are plain characters in quotes.

commandLines.name: powershell-launcher-status
commandLines.purpose: A PowerShell login: every element single-quoted, and the call operator in front so a quoted path is run, not printed.

commandLines.name: powershell-single-quote
commandLines.purpose: A single quote inside a PowerShell single-quoted string is written twice.

commandLines.name: powershell-typographic-quotes
commandLines.purpose: U+2018 to U+201B are single quotes to the PowerShell tokenizer, so each is doubled like U+0027. Doubling only the ASCII quote let one of these end the string early (T11, A12).

commandLines.name: powershell-variable-literal
commandLines.purpose: Nothing expands inside single quotes: $env:USERPROFILE reaches the agent as those sixteen characters.

commandLines.name: powershell-stop-parsing
commandLines.purpose: PowerShell treats --% as its stop-parsing token even quoted, so every later argument would arrive unquoted; it is refused.

commandLines.name: powershell-trailing-backslash
commandLines.purpose: Windows PowerShell 5.1 passes a quoted native argument with a trailing backslash without doubling it, so the argument swallows the next one.

commandLines.name: powershell-double-space
commandLines.purpose: Two spaces in a row are refused: PowerShell legacy native-argument passing does not keep them reliably.

commandLines.name: powershell-double-quote
commandLines.purpose: A double quote inside a native argument is mangled by legacy argument passing.

commandLines.name: powershell-empty-element
commandLines.purpose: Windows PowerShell drops an empty native argument altogether; it is refused instead.

classifications.name: exit-127-sh-not-found
classifications.purpose: A shell that could not find the interpreter exits 127 with nothing on stdout: the agent never started, so another system may be tried (A4).

classifications.name: exit-127-fish-unknown-command

classifications.name: exit-126-permission-denied

classifications.name: exit-127-blank-crlf-stdout
classifications.purpose: Blank means tab, LF, CR and space only, so a stray CRLF on stdout is still blank.

classifications.name: exit-127-with-output
classifications.purpose: Exit 127 with something on stdout: something ran, so it is not the shell failing to start it.

classifications.name: powershell-term-not-recognized
classifications.purpose: PowerShell exits 1 for a missing command, and 1 is also what the agent exits with, so the text names the failure without making it never.

classifications.name: cmd-path-not-found
classifications.purpose: cmd could not find a path: named for a person, still unknown.

input.stderr: The system cannot find the path specified.

classifications.name: cannot-find-module
classifications.purpose: Node ran and the entry is missing. A mutation is not tried on another system on the strength of stderr text (A4).

classifications.name: err-module-not-found
classifications.purpose: The ESM spelling of a missing module.

classifications.name: no-such-file
classifications.purpose: exit 1 with "No such file or directory": nothing in the table, so it is unreadable output.

input.stderr: bash: /home/me/missing: No such file or directory

classifications.name: exit-0-empty
classifications.purpose: Exit 0 with no output at all: the agent always answers with JSON, so this is not a reply.

classifications.name: not-json-braces
classifications.purpose: Braces that do not hold JSON are not a reply.

classifications.name: reply-exit-0
classifications.purpose: A JSON object on stdout is a reply, whatever else is true.

classifications.name: reply-exit-255
classifications.purpose: A reboot drops the link after the agent answered; the reply on stdout wins over the 255.

classifications.name: reply-exit-1
classifications.purpose: ok false is still a reply: the agent answered.

classifications.name: reply-after-clixml
classifications.purpose: Windows PowerShell can print a #< CLIXML banner first; the object from the first { to the last } is the reply.

classifications.name: reply-after-timeout
classifications.purpose: The watchdog fired after the agent had already answered: the answer counts.

classifications.name: no-exit-status-blank
classifications.purpose: The channel closed without an exit status: the link was lost, and nothing says when.

classifications.name: no-exit-status-reply
classifications.purpose: No exit status, but a reply arrived before the link went: it is a reply.

classifications.name: launch-failed
classifications.purpose: ssh could not be started at all: nothing can have been sent.

classifications.name: timed-out
classifications.purpose: The client stopped the process: the command may be running.

walks.name: mutation-stops-after-unexplained-255
walks.purpose: An unexplained 255 may have run the restart, so the mutation goes nowhere else: exactly one attempt across two routes and two systems (M15).

walks.name: mutation-fails-over-after-refusal
walks.purpose: A refusal in the ssh log proves nothing was sent, so the mutation moves on; the refusal is route-level, so the rest of that route is skipped.

walks.name: mutation-next-system-after-127
walks.purpose: Exit 127 with blank stdout means the interpreter never started: the same route's other system is tried (A4).

walks.name: mutation-stops-after-cannot-find-module
walks.purpose: Node ran and printed "Cannot find module". stderr text never makes a mutation safe to resend (A4).

walks.name: mutation-stops-after-powershell-not-recognized
walks.purpose: PowerShell's "not recognized" comes with exit 1, which the agent also uses: stopped.

walks.name: mutation-stops-after-unreadable-output
walks.purpose: Output nobody can read was still output: the command ran, and is reconciled with op, never resent.

walks.name: mutation-stops-after-watchdog
walks.purpose: The client's own watchdog fired: the work may be running.

walks.name: mutation-continues-after-bad-request
walks.purpose: A line refused before sending was never sent, so the next system is tried.

walks.name: mutation-exhausted-when-nothing-was-sent
walks.purpose: Every attempt failed before dispatch: the walk runs out with nothing sent anywhere.

walks.name: read-continues-after-unexplained-255
walks.purpose: A read is safe to repeat, so it goes on; a lost link is route-level, so it moves to the next route.

walks.name: read-continues-after-cannot-find-module
walks.purpose: A missing module is not route-level: a read tries the same route's next system.

walks.name: read-exhausted-after-route-failures
walks.purpose: A changed host key kills the lan route, its other system is skipped, and authentication fails on the next route.

statusBudgets.name: first-attempt-full-deadline
statusBudgets.purpose: A fresh 30 s status: the agent gets its full 20 s.

statusBudgets.name: cap-holds-with-time-to-spare
statusBudgets.purpose: Never more than 20 s, however much time is left.

statusBudgets.name: second-attempt-exactly-enough
statusBudgets.purpose: 25 s left: 20 s for the agent and 5 s in hand.

statusBudgets.name: second-attempt-one-short
statusBudgets.purpose: One millisecond less: the budget shrinks with the time left.

statusBudgets.name: third-attempt-after-two-dead-routes
statusBudgets.purpose: Two dead routes left 14 s. Sending 20000 here made the agent overrun the client's own deadline (C9).

statusBudgets.name: floor-for-a-later-attempt
statusBudgets.purpose: Exactly 1 s left after the margin: still worth an attempt.

statusBudgets.name: no-later-attempt-without-time
statusBudgets.purpose: Less than 1 s left after the margin, and an attempt was already made: stop.

statusBudgets.name: first-attempt-always-goes
statusBudgets.purpose: The first attempt goes out whatever is left, with the 1 s floor.

hosts.name: host-space
hosts.purpose: A space splits the host into two arguments.

hosts.name: host-semicolon
hosts.purpose: A semicolon is shell syntax.

hosts.name: host-bracketed-ipv6
hosts.purpose: Brackets are known_hosts syntax for a port; a pin pattern is built from the checked bare address instead.

hosts.name: host-scheme
hosts.purpose: A URL is not a host.

hosts.name: host-user-at-host
hosts.purpose: A user belongs in user; an @ in the host would change which account ssh logs in to.

hosts.name: host-empty-label
hosts.purpose: Two dots in a row leave an empty label.

hosts.name: host-leading-dot
hosts.purpose: A name cannot start with a dot.

hosts.name: host-trailing-dot
hosts.purpose: A trailing dot passes the document guard and is not dialled: names are written without it.

hosts.name: host-label-ends-with-hyphen
hosts.purpose: A label cannot end with a hyphen.

hosts.name: host-octet-over-255
hosts.purpose: All digits in the last label make it an address, and 256 is no octet.

hosts.name: host-three-octets
hosts.purpose: Three octets would be completed by a resolver into an address nobody wrote.

hosts.name: host-all-digits
hosts.purpose: A single all-digit label is an integer address to a resolver.

hosts.name: host-leading-zero-octet
hosts.purpose: A leading zero reads as octal to some resolvers.

hosts.name: host-ipv6-zone
hosts.purpose: A zone names an interface of the device that wrote it; it means nothing elsewhere.

hosts.name: host-ipv6-two-compressions
hosts.purpose: Two :: are ambiguous.

hosts.name: host-ipv4-then-compression
hosts.purpose: An embedded IPv4 address must be the last group.

hosts.name: host-host-with-port
hosts.purpose: A port belongs in port.

hosts.name: host-label-too-long
hosts.purpose: A 64-character label is one over the limit.

hosts.name: host-name-too-long
hosts.purpose: 254 characters is one over the limit.

hosts.name: host-non-ascii-name
hosts.purpose: Names are ASCII; an internationalised name is written in its punycode form.

users.name: user-plain
users.purpose: A local account name in lower case.

users.name: user-dotted
users.purpose: Dots are allowed inside a name.

users.name: user-leading-underscore
users.purpose: A service account starting with an underscore.

users.name: user-email-style
users.purpose: A Microsoft account login on Windows.

users.name: user-domain-backslash
users.purpose: A domain account, DOMAIN\name.

users.name: user-single-space
users.purpose: A Windows display-style account name with one space.

users.name: user-one-character
users.purpose: One character is a name.

users.name: user-empty
users.purpose: Nothing at all is not a login name.

users.name: user-option
users.purpose: A leading hyphen would be read as an ssh option.

users.name: user-semicolon
users.purpose: A semicolon is shell syntax.

users.name: user-command-substitution
users.purpose: A command substitution.

users.name: user-single-quote
users.purpose: A quote would end a quoted run on the remote side.

users.name: user-double-space
users.purpose: Two spaces in a row are refused.

users.name: user-space-then-hyphen
users.purpose: A space followed by a hyphen looks like an option to whatever splits on spaces.

users.name: user-leading-space
users.purpose: A name starts with a letter, digit or underscore.

users.name: user-trailing-space
users.purpose: A name ends with a letter, digit, dot, underscore or hyphen.

users.name: user-trailing-backslash
users.purpose: A trailing backslash would escape whatever follows it.

users.name: user-trailing-at
users.purpose: An @ at the end leaves an empty host.

users.name: user-too-long
users.purpose: 65 characters is one over the limit.

users.name: user-non-ascii
users.purpose: Login names are ASCII here.

ports.name: port-lowest
ports.purpose: Port 1 is the lowest port there is.

ports.name: port-ssh
ports.purpose: The ssh port, the one nearly every endpoint uses.

ports.name: port-negative
ports.purpose: A negative number is no port.

ports.name: port-string
ports.purpose: A port is a JSON integer, never a string that looks like one.
